note: Adapted from Emerson's 1960 species description (in English), published in American Museum Novitates 1988 (pp. 1–49); the species description begins on p. 16 (soldier, Table 3), p. 17 gives the comparisons and type material, and the genus characters on pp. 12–15. Only the soldier and worker are described; no alate was seen. The worker morphology is given only in the genus characters (p. 14) without a species-level description, so no separate worker section is given. Measurements are taken from Table 3 on p. 16, with sample sizes (No.) copied as they stand. The base copy _tmp/fleet_01/pdf4/emerson1960-sixgenera.pdf has no text layer (PyMuPDF extracted only 481 characters), so the text was entered from the OCR of the archive.org scan of the same journal (identifier sixnewgenerater1988emer), and Table 3's 11 sets of values were cross-checked page by page against the local PDF with tesseract, the two results agreeing.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head width 1.35—1.50 mm, head length including mandibles 3.23—3.47 mm, pronotum width 0.69—0.75 mm. Larger than the congener M. heterochilus (Silvestri), whose soldier head width is 1.10 mm, with a weaker median elevation of the posterior part of the postmentum, a shallower emargination of the anterior margin of the labrum, blunter lateral points of the labrum, a shallower lateral emargination behind the labral points, the elbow of the mandible closer to the base, and a deeper emargination of the anterior margin of the pronotum. No alate described.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head brownish yellow, pronotum generally paler than the head, legs and abdomen paler than the pronotum. Vertex and sides with a few scattered bristles and short hairs, very few short hairs near the opening of the fontanelle; the lateral elevation below and behind the antennal socket usually bears one bristle. Postmentum without hairs or bristles. Anterior margin of the labrum with several bristles on each side. Pronotum with several bristles laterally and posteriorly, but the anterior margin bears only short hairs in most specimens, with 1—2 bristles in a few. Abdominal tergites and sternites each with a row of marginal bristles; tergites with a few short hairs laterally; sternites with several short hairs, not forming a felt. Antennae 14 or 15-segmented: when 15, segment 3 much shorter than segment 2 or 4; when 14, segment 3 equal to segment 2 and slightly longer than segment 4. Other characters as in the genus. Measurements (mm, sample size in parentheses): head length including mandibles 3.23—3.47 (n=2); head length to lateral base of mandible 1.59—1.76 (n=11); head width 1.35—1.50 (n=11); head thickness including postmentum 1.30—1.44 (n=11); median postmentum length 0.93—1.00 (n=4); greatest width of median postmentum 0.37—0.43 (n=11); width between labral points 0.40—0.47 (n=10); left mandible length 1.68—1.85 (n=11); pronotum length 0.30—0.32 (n=7); pronotum width 0.69—0.75 (n=11); hind tibia length 1.03—1.18 (n=11).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type material: holotype and paratypes totalling 6 soldiers and 1 worker, collected 20 May 1948 by A. Emerson on the ground at Pygmy camp 4 km north of Camp Putnam, Epulu River, Belgian Congo (1°24′N, 28°36′E); paratype series of 5 soldiers and 2 workers collected 29 May 1948 at Yangambi (0°47′N, 24°23′E) from the outer layer of an earth ridge at a tree base occupied by Protermes prorepens (Sjöstedt). The species is named for Fairfield Osborn, president of the New York Zoological Society. The genus also contains M. heterochilus (Silvestri) and an undescribed species from French Guinea.
